title: PINES Management Processes — Reporting and Administrative Tools
scope: Reporting, analysis, batch administrative utilities and supporting infrastructure used by PINES staff, managers and administrators to manage collections, patrons, transactions and financial records across the consortium. This specification covers report content, batch item utilities, data access controls, operational constraints (OS, browsers, accessibility), and developer-provided metadata/documentation. It does not redefine OPAC patron-facing features except where reports read OPAC-created data.

glossary.definition: A saved, administrator-managed report definition that staff can run as-is or (where allowed) clone and modify.
A report run as an asynchronous job on the server or reporting subsystem that does not block interactive clients.
A batch operation that moves item records from one location to another (for pull lists, outreach, mobile libraries, temporary events, etc.).
An item or bibliographic instance that, within the chosen scope (library or system), is the only copy owned by that scope.
Online Public Access Catalog — the patron-facing web/catalog interface that creates holds and transactions which reports may read.

requirements.name: Material volume reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide reports that show the volume of material for a selected library or group of libraries at any point in time, including counts for new acquisitions, items on shelf (checked in) and items out in circulation, and allow breaking down results by category (examples: total items, holds count, adult fiction, board books). Categories shall be configurable per library and templates shall be able to expose custom categories for reuse. Additionally, the reporting capability shall explicitly support analysis of the collection and its use by patrons (circulation patterns and item-level usage) so catalogers and managers can evaluate collection use and inform acquisitions, redistribution and weeding decisions; this analysis must be possible at branch and system scopes and be exportable for further offline analysis. (Sources: DOC-001, DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Direct stakeholder request as a key monthly/board reporting need and repeated endorsement across working-group documents; added patron-usage analysis is similarly essential for collection management.

requirements.name: System capacity interface
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a high-level interface displaying capacity and key metrics for all branches at once, with the ability to drill down to individual branch detail, sort and filter by region, library type or current load, display trend data (growth/shrink patterns), and export results to CSV for directors. The interface shall support grouping of locations where necessary to avoid overwhelming displays. In addition to the original capacity and trend features, the interface shall explicitly support analysis of branch capacity and optimal distribution of the collection (views and reports that help plan redistribution and placement of material across branches) to aid operational planning and collection balance decisions. (Sources: DOC-002, DOC-010, DOC-018)
requirements.priority_reason: Expressed as a system-level need for cross-branch planning and explicitly requested by multiple stakeholders; branch-capacity analysis is an operational priority.

requirements.name: Shelf-space utilization report
requirements.explanation: The system shall produce a shelf-space report, per selected library or for the system, that compares for each genre and format: percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space; the report shall support side-by-side comparison across libraries and date-range filtering. Because shelf space may not be tracked directly, the requirement allows use of calculated estimates (e.g., item dimensions or item-count proxies) and requires the report to document the estimation method used. (Sources: DOC-003, DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Cataloging and collection managers requested this to support weeding/space decisions, and stakeholders emphasized per-branch and system views.

requirements.name: Batch item transfer utility
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a batch item transfer utility that allows staff with appropriate permissions to: build queries for candidate materials (and save those queries as templates), manually select items from query results, change selected items' location fields for transfer, generate pull/transit lists (printable), and optionally schedule or execute an automatic revert to original location based on elapsed time or event criteria. The utility shall support preview and confirmation before applying changes, an undo mechanism where feasible, printable transit labels and transfer delay alerts, and shall record transfer history for each item. Batch updates shall use transaction-safe processing and be efficient for very large collections. (Sources: DOC-004, DOC-010, DOC-015, DOC-019)
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple cataloging and branch staff identified this as critical for outreach, mobile services, and routine redistribution; technical staff noted batch/transaction safety is essential.

requirements.name: Missing, damaged and in-transit reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide two related reports: (a) missing and damaged items report by branch with optional inclusion of condition notes (e.g., 'water damage', 'vandalism') and time-range filtering for trend analysis; and (b) an in-transit items report that lists items that have been in-transit more than X days (X configurable, default suggested 7 days), merging both transit-to and transit-from perspectives and allowing sorting by due date to prioritize follow-up. Both reports shall be runnable per branch and system-wide and shall support the specific operational need to list missing/damaged items per branch and to list items in-transit beyond a configurable threshold.
requirements.priority_reason: Front-line and delivery staff repeatedly requested both reports to manage inventory, reduce losses, and coordinate deliveries.

requirements.name: Item record purging and last-copy protection
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide reports and a safety-controlled utility to identify item records for purging using customizable criteria (status, time in status, last circulation dates, combinations of criteria), assist with batch status conversions, and provide an efficient mechanism to delete volume and copy entries and orphan bibliographic records. Critically, the system shall produce a 'last copy report' that flags items which are the last copy within a chosen scope (branch or system) so catalogers can avoid accidental deletion. Purging operations shall be driven from read-only candidate reports, require a separate explicit confirmation step, and create an audit trail recording who performed actions and when. The utility may be schedulable for recurring runs but must protect against accidental mass deletion. The requirement explicitly covers the requested utility and reports for identifying purge candidates based on customizable criteria such as status.
requirements.priority_reason: Cataloging and collection staff defined this as critical (last-copy protection named 'CRITICAL'), and stakeholders required safety/audit controls.

requirements.name: Deletion-audit and deletion reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall log all successful and attempted (denied) deletions of records (item, patron, bibliographic) to an audit table via database triggers or equivalent, capturing record type, record identifier, user who attempted the deletion, timestamp, and the operator's location; a report interface shall enable aggregation of deletions by period, by user, by location and by type for auditing and compliance. The reporting capability must support counting and tracking deletions per location and for the system as a whole to support local and consortium-level audits.
requirements.priority_reason: Stakeholders require traceability for accountability and compliance; technical staff indicated database triggers are feasible and necessary.

requirements.name: Patron characteristics and demographic queries
requirements.explanation: The system shall support limiting and grouping queries and reports by patron characteristics including configurable age ranges, zip code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language; it must support combined filters with AND/OR logic and include records with null/missing values rather than implicitly excluding them. Further, the reporting capability shall explicitly provide demographic-analysis facilities to support program planning (for example, cohort or zip/county-level breakdowns, configurable age-range buckets and language-based groupings) so outreach and program planners can target services based on patron population characteristics. (Sources: DOC-008, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Program planners and outreach staff explicitly requested these filters and groupings for program targeting; configurability and inclusion of nulls were emphasized and demographic-analysis support is similarly critical for planning.

requirements.name: Inactive patrons reporting and outreach export
requirements.explanation: The system shall generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity in the last X days, where X is configurable (supporting at least 30, 90, 180, 365 and arbitrary values) and the report can be scoped to System, Home Library, County or other levels. The report shall optionally include current mailing addresses, flag or separate patrons with outstanding fines, allow exclusion rules (do-not-disturb, VIPs, staff, opt-outs), be exportable to CSV and be runnable as a background job for large patron sets. (Sources: DOC-009, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple libraries run these reports routinely for database cleanup and outreach; performance concerns require background processing.

requirements.name: Operating environment and scalability
requirements.explanation: The system shall support a consortium-scale environment (example scale: 286 locations, ~17M annual circulations, large acquisition volumes), operate on Linux or Solaris servers, be usable via web-browser or Windows client, support IE 6.0+ and Firefox 2.0+ where web-based, and ensure report processing can occur without disrupting OPAC or circulation clients (by background processing, replicas or other architectural separation). The reporting and management processes must not constrain OPAC responsiveness or availability during peak operational periods, and shall explicitly document the supported server operating systems (Linux or Solaris) and architectural separation options (background jobs, reporting replicas or equivalent) used to prevent user-facing disruption. In addition, the specification shall record the deployment/operational assumption that Management Processes are consolidated at a central location and accept input from and provide services to multiple branches/locations (so design, capacity planning and failover considerations assume centralized management-process endpoints); this centralization assumption must be documented alongside the described architectural separation options so implementers and operators understand where services are hosted and how that affects latency, access control and scaling across the consortium.
requirements.priority_reason: Technical constraints and scale were repeatedly called out by IT stakeholders and working-group materials; non-disruption of OPAC is essential to operations.

requirements.name: Accessibility, standards and platform constraints
requirements.explanation: The system shall comply with accessibility requirements (support screen readers, screen magnification and other assistive technologies and produce standards-compliant HTML), use a fully relational database back-end, and provide development/training environments with migration capability to production. The reporting subsystem shall not constrain OPAC functionality or responsiveness. In keeping with stakeholder accessibility requirements, management processes shall explicitly be usable with screen-reading and screen-magnification software and other assistive technologies and shall produce standards-compliant HTML to permit assistive tools to function. The vendor shall explicitly document the use of a fully relational database back-end and shall provide mechanisms to migrate configurations and artifacts (export/import of templates, permission settings, saved queries and other configuration items) between development, training and production environments to support safe testing and staged rollouts; this migration capability must be described in developer and operational documentation so administrators can reproduce configurations across environments.
requirements.priority_reason: Legal accessibility obligations and architectural constraints were explicitly stated by multiple stakeholders and technical staff; compliance is essential.

requirements.name: Developer-provided data specifications, process descriptions and help
requirements.explanation: The developer shall supply comprehensive data specifications (field names, types and relationships) for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request and other records used by management reports; a high-level description of major processes (imports/exports, validation flows) and an online, hierarchical, cross-linked HTML help system. Error reporting shall include high-level and low-level, query-specific feedback for administrators. Concretely, the developer-supplied materials must include complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item and hold/request records, high-level descriptions of import/export and validation processes (including bibliographic record import/export and validation against authority sources), and an online hierarchical HTML help system that documents and illustrates management-reporting features and common administrative workflows. The system shall provide thorough front-end error reporting and feedback for Local and Global System Administrators, including both high-level user-facing messages and low-level, query-specific diagnostic feedback accessible from the administrative interface so administrators can diagnose and correct malformed queries, data-mapping problems, import/export failures and similar issues without relying solely on back-end logs. The developer documentation must describe error message formats and where detailed diagnostics are surfaced in the UI.
requirements.priority_reason: Staff need documentation and meaningful error feedback to author and troubleshoot reports; developer-provided specs, process descriptions and help were repeatedly required.

requirements.name: Query tool and open-template reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a user-friendly query/report designer across all record types (bib, item, patron, transaction, financial) that supports field selection, picklists, Boolean logic (AND/OR), configurable regular-expression use where appropriate, saved queries, and an 'open template' mode exposing all attributes for filtering and display. The open-template mode must expose attributes associated with circulation, patrons, items, bills and bibliographic records for both filtering and display so advanced users can construct fine-grained reports; administrators shall be able to restrict access to tables/fields. This capability must explicitly support the fine-grained reporting requirements described in stakeholder materials (Appendix-style fine-grained report support).
requirements.priority_reason: Repeated user demand for a flexible query designer and open-template reporting across multiple documents and survey results; fine-grained access is required for advanced administrative reporting.

requirements.name: Report templates, permissions and shared folders
requirements.explanation: Administrators shall be able to create, publish and manage report templates; templates must be runnable as-is, clonable for modification, and support administrator limits on which filters/display fields can be altered. The system shall support fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning and running reports, and shared folders to manage access by role, workgroup or individual. Role-assignments must be administrable so permission changes follow role changes. The specification shall explicitly require fine-grained controls limiting who can create and clone reports and shall require shared-folder semantics that allow administrators to grant or deny execution, cloning or editing rights on specific templates or folders of templates to particular roles, workgroups or individuals; these shared-folder permissions must be documentable and manageable via the administrative UI so template visibility and editability can be maintained across organizational changes.
requirements.priority_reason: High priority across stakeholders for consistent board reports, controlled templates, and easy admin of permissions.

requirements.name: Report scheduling, queue visibility, prioritization and cancellation
requirements.explanation: The system shall allow reports to be scheduled (ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly), run as background jobs, show queue position and status (waiting, running, completed, failed) to requestors, allow certain reports to be prioritized to jump ahead in queue, and permit cancellation of scheduled or running reports. Administrators shall be able to configure recurring reports and their recipients. The system must ensure reports can be queued and processed in the background to avoid disruption during open hours and shall provide queue visibility to requestors so users know expected completion or position. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-012, DOC-019, DOC-020, DOC-016)
requirements.priority_reason: Queue visibility and prioritization were repeatedly reported as operational needs to prevent user confusion and support directors' reporting needs; background processing to avoid disruption is high priority.

requirements.name: Report output formats, delivery and export
requirements.explanation: Reports shall be exportable in CSV and HTML formats and provide reliable Excel-compatible output (or Excel export) for downstream use (pivot tables). The system shall support emailing report results to specified addresses (address book supported) and include the report selection criteria and report name in outputs. Export formats must preserve all null/blank fields and produce pivot-table-capable output. In particular, the vendor must support CSV exports explicitly to meet directors' spreadsheet needs and to permit integration with outreach systems that ingest CSV data. The system shall therefore explicitly document the supported export formats (CSV, HTML, and Excel-compatible output) and confirm preservation of null/blank fields in CSV exports.
requirements.priority_reason: Export and delivery features are important for directors and integrations; they were requested frequently but are not safety-critical relative to core reporting.

requirements.name: Historical reporting and reporting warehouse
requirements.explanation: The system shall support historical reporting requirements (snapshots for given dates/date ranges). Where required for performance and reproducible historical snapshots, a reporting warehouse or other archival mechanism shall be provided to retain historical state separate from production row-level changes. The system shall indicate whether a result is from a historical snapshot or real-time data. The reporting capability must explicitly support both historical (warehouse/snapshot) queries and real-time reporting modes; the system shall document which mode produced a given result and provide the historical-warehouse option for date-or-date-range selection as requested by stakeholders, and shall identify reports that must be run in real-time (for example, 'what's overdue today') versus those that may rely on snapshots.
requirements.priority_reason: Users requested historical snapshots and technical staff indicated a warehouse may be required to provide this reliably without impacting production; supporting both real-time and historical modes addresses both operational and reporting needs.

requirements.name: Transaction reporting and types
requirements.explanation: The system shall retain transaction history for a configurable period (transaction history retained X days configurable) while keeping monthly and annual aggregates indefinitely, and provide reports that group transactions by hour, terminal, branch and system; count types of check-in (book-drop, by terminal, by user/self-service) and check-out (staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self renewal, online renewals) individually and cumulatively; and produce transaction reports (holds placed, holds filled, check-outs) per patron, per library, per selected group, per system, or per county. Transaction reporting shall include activity reports that indicate traffic and volume of use (check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, holds filled) and support cross-tabulation across axes such as terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type and patron location to support detailed analysis. Archival and transaction-warehouse behavior for retained transactions must support anonymization or other measures required to protect patron privacy per applicable State Law while still providing useful demographic statistics and aggregates for planning and reporting. The system shall also provide holds-specific reporting and allow these reports at branch and system scope. Additionally, the reporting capability shall provide staff-productivity and workflow analysis derived from transaction metrics (for example, per-terminal and per-staff activity, time-based throughput metrics and comparisons) so managers can assess staffing and workflow efficiency; such staff-productivity reports must respect privacy/anonymization rules where required. (Sources: DOC-001, DOC-010, DOC-019)
requirements.priority_reason: Detailed transaction counting and grouping are core reporting needs used daily by branches and managers, and staff-productivity analysis is operationally important for staffing and workflow decisions.

requirements.name: Financial reporting and audit trail
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide financial reports including value-of-items aggregations (using purchase price fields) for an entire collection or a selected portion, patron account balances by patron/home library/system, fines and charges accrued per period and per type, fines waived per period and branch, and payments by period and payment method. The system shall maintain an auditable ledger of patron payments that records which charges payments are applied to and shall support reconciliation and compliance with applicable accounting/archival retention policies. The reporting capability must explicitly include the ability to generate item-value reports (aggregated value of items for a given scope), support queries for patron accounts with balances greater than a configurable threshold (to identify accounts needing attention), and ensure reports and data archiving comply with standard accounting practice and applicable state, county and municipal auditing requirements. This requirement therefore also covers the system ability to track and verify financial transactions end-to-end (payment application, reconciliation and reporting) as an auditable function. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-019)
requirements.priority_reason: Finance stakeholders explicitly required value and ledger capabilities and legal/audit compliance; tracking/verification of transactions is essential for accounting integrity.

requirements.name: Canned, on-demand and open-template report interfaces
requirements.explanation: The system shall support three reporting interfaces: canned report templates (predefined templates runnable ASAP or scheduled), on-demand editable reports for preset categories, and open-template reporting exposing all attributes for advanced ad-hoc queries. Administrators shall be able to create, publish and manage report templates; templates must be runnable as-is, clonable for modification, and support administrator limits on which filters/display fields can be altered. Canned reports shall be discoverable with descriptive hover pop-ups and a delivered set of pre-written templates (including pre-defined board/external-consumer templates); canned templates shall support running by yesterday's data, last week, last month or last year. The specification shall explicitly require a delivered set of pre-defined board reports (for consumption by library boards and other external consumers) that expose the basic statistics required by common state reporting (for example, the Georgia Annual Report), and the canned interface shall support both immediate (ASAP) execution and recurring schedules as part of the shipped product.
requirements.priority_reason: Stakeholders asked for distinct modes (canned, on-demand, open-template) to cover common and ad-hoc needs; canned/pre-defined board reports were repeatedly requested for governance and external consumption.

requirements.name: Uncataloged material inventory and counting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a minimal-labor workflow to record, distribute and count uncataloged material (e.g., paperback/children's board books) so those transactions contribute to circulation statistics and can be identified in reports while avoiding full cataloging overhead. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple branches identified uncataloged material handling as a practical need for rapid distribution and counting.

requirements.name: Data quality and bibliographic integrity reports
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide data quality reports for identifying bibliographic and item anomalies such as bibliographic records with no volumes attached, records missing specific MARC fields, items with invalid item type or excessively long call numbers, items with zero use count or candidate weeding lists, and a mechanism to retrieve last-edit and last-circulation metadata separately. These outputs shall support generation of weeding candidate lists and related analytics so cataloging staff can perform weeding workflows efficiently; weeding reports shall be easy to run and export and shall be identified as frequently used operational reports. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-015, DOC-020, DOC-018)
requirements.priority_reason: Cataloging staff require specialized data-quality and weeding reporting to maintain catalog integrity and support routine weeding decisions; users identified these as frequently used.

requirements.name: Authentication and role-based access control
requirements.explanation: The system shall support streamlined but optional staff login mechanisms (e.g., card-swipe) and also traditional username/password; every login must identify which staff member is logged in for auditing. User rights shall be defined and administered via roles/security groups (Staff, Local Admin, Library Manager, Global Admin) to simplify permission changes and to control report and template operations. Access control must support assignment at multiple granularities including individuals, workgroups and arbitrary staff groups so administrators can target permissions to operational groupings, and the system shall provide easy-to-use administrative facilities for creating, editing and reassigning roles and permissions to follow staff and organizational changes. The administrative facilities shall make it straightforward to change an individual's effective permissions by modifying their role assignments (so permission changes can be managed via role edits rather than per-user edits), and the system shall record role-assignment changes for audit purposes.
requirements.priority_reason: Operational security, auditability and local administrative ease were emphasized repeatedly; ease of role administration and flexible access groups are essential for day-to-day operations.

requirements.name: Miscellaneous quick-access and fine-grained features
requirements.explanation: The system shall support assorted usability and integration items requested repeatedly: ability to include selection criteria in outputs (report results shall display the date selection criteria and report name at the top or bottom of outputs to clarify context), upload text files (barcodes/TCNs) to filter reports, allow pivot-compatible exports, allow retrieval of MARC fields in single-row outputs, allow report result comparison columns (month-over-month, percent change), and provide an address-book for delivery recipients. The specification requires visible inclusion of the selection criteria in generated outputs to aid consumers in interpreting exported reports; consequently, the system shall provide the query selections along with results so users can see which filters or selections produced the returned rows. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: These features improve day-to-day usability for report consumers and were frequently requested; inclusion of query selections with results prevents misinterpretation of exported reports.

blacklist.name: Document Reports Functionality
blacklist.statement: Document optimal Reports functionality within a future Evergreen release and develop a list of requirements.
blacklist.reason: This is a working-group/project activity (documenting optimal functionality and developing a requirements list) rather than a runtime software requirement that the product must implement. Project planning and requirements-compilation tasks belong to program process artifacts, not the management-processes feature set.

blacklist.name: Reports Testing Group
blacklist.statement: Become the Reports testing group, through which all new Reports development would be filtered.
blacklist.reason: This describes an organizational/testing-group responsibility and process for development governance, not a software capability to be implemented in the product.

blacklist.name: Compile Executive Reports
blacklist.statement: Compile a list of reports needed for an Executive Reports Interface.
blacklist.reason: Compiling a list of required reports is a planning/delivery activity for stakeholders, not an implementation-level software requirement. The produced executive reports themselves are in scope when specified as templates; the act of compiling is out of scope.

blacklist.name: Determine Templates
blacklist.statement: Determine and create templates needed for all PINES libraries.
blacklist.reason: Determining and creating templates is an operational/content-preparation activity (work to be done by staff or project teams). The underlying capability to create, publish and manage templates is already captured in the specification; this candidate is a project task, not a new runtime requirement.

blacklist.name: Iterative UI Specification
blacklist.statement: Specify user interface details using an iterative, prototype-oriented methodology as development progresses.
blacklist.reason: This describes a development methodology for designing the UI (an engineering process), not a runtime functional requirement for the management processes product. UI design approach is outside the scope of the product's functional requirements.

open_questions.question: How should 'shelf space' be calculated when no explicit shelf-space field exists?
open_questions.reason: Stakeholders require a shelf-space percentage metric but multiple sources note the database does not track shelf space directly. The specification permits estimation but the exact algorithm (item dimensions, per-format average linear inches, or item-count proxy) was not decided.

open_questions.question: What scope and definitive metric(s) define 'capacity' for the capacity interface (e.g., physical shelf linear-feet, configured item limits, circulation processing capacity)?
open_questions.reason: Participants requested a system-wide capacity dashboard but asked different questions about what 'capacity' means. Implementation requires a stakeholder decision to select concrete metrics to display.

open_questions.question: Which archival retention policy values shall the system enforce by default (e.g., transaction retention X days, financial archival years)?
open_questions.reason: Documents reference configurable retention and an example 7-year finance retention but did not lock specific defaults; this requires policy decision for defaults and guidance for configuration.

open_questions.question: For auto-revert of transferred items: which event triggers or precedence rules should be supported (time-based first, event-based overrides, checked-out at destination to cancel auto-revert)?
open_questions.reason: Stakeholders asked for both time-based and event-based auto-revert behaviors, but interactions and precedence (e.g., revert after X days unless checked out at destination) were not fully specified.

open_questions.question: Should historical reporting use a separate reporting replica with periodic snapshots, or a dedicated reporting warehouse mirroring the production schema?
open_questions.reason: Technical staff raised performance and reproducibility concerns; choice affects architecture, latency and complexity.
